purpose: Nateglinide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works best when used along with a healthy diet and exercise. It is not used for type 1 diabetes or diabetic emergencies.
how_it_works: Nateglinide works by telling your pancreas to release insulin quickly right after you eat a meal. It acts fast and for a short time, so it mainly helps with the blood sugar spike that happens after eating. Think of it as a quick helper that jumps into action when you start your meal.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can make you feel shaky, sweaty, dizzy, or confused. You may also notice mild weight gain, a runny nose or cold-like symptoms, back pain, or joint aches. Most side effects are mild.
warnings: Do not skip meals after taking this medication, as it can cause dangerously low blood sugar. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as this medicine may not be safe for you. Avoid drinking excessive alcohol, which can worsen low blood sugar. Let all your doctors and your pharmacist know you take this medicine, especially before any surgery.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 120 mg taken by mouth 1 to 30 minutes before each main meal (breakfast, lunch, and dinner). If you skip a meal, skip that dose too. Your doctor may start you at 60 mg if your blood sugar is close to your target goal. Never take it more than 30 minutes before eating.
